comment: Read receipt disclosure policy and per-scope client preference vectors. Spec: discovery/read-receipts.md §2.4-§2.5 and discovery/client-preferences.md §3.6. Disclosure policy is a soft (non-cryptographic) commitment carried by the component cell ak.component.realm.read_receipt_policy.v1 using sequenced_state. Track-level read-receipt overrides are absent; a discussion timeline that needs a distinct policy uses an independent Strand/Circle scope. Signal payload kind and event_id remain encrypted, so Sync Service enforces only signed scope fanout while compliant clients enforce generation, display, and referenced-sender filtering. User preferences live under the actor-private account-data key ak.read_receipt.preferences. The decision rule is: required > disabled > optional defers to (strand → realm → default).

vectors.name: disclosure_required_locks_client_send
vectors.comment: When a Realm declares disclosure=required, even a user preference of send=false MUST be overridden — compliant clients send the receipt and lock the UI toggle.

vectors.name: disclosure_disabled_is_enforced_by_clients
vectors.comment: When a Realm declares disclosure=disabled, even a user preference of send=true MUST be overridden. A compliant sender does not generate the receipt; a receiving client drops a non-compliant receipt after decryption. Sync Service cannot distinguish it from another encrypted Signal payload and only enforces scope fanout.

vectors.name: visibility_private_filters_after_client_decryption
vectors.comment: When visibility=private, Sync Service still fans out only by the signed outer scope because event_id is encrypted. After decryption, only the client that sent the referenced event may display the receipt; other scope members drop it.

vectors.name: display_false_hides_local_indicator_only
vectors.comment: When display=false, the client hides other members' read-receipt indicator locally only. The preference MUST NOT change whether this actor sends receipts, Sync Service fanout, unread accounting, or private read cursors.

vectors.name: branch_overrides_tighten_only
vectors.comment: A Strand/Circle scope (upgraded discussion timeline, Strand.scope_circle_id binding) MAY tighten the parent Realm's read-receipt policy only when scope_overrides_allowed=true. Optional → Disabled at the Strand/Circle scope is a privacy tightening, Members → Private is also a visibility tightening (smaller audience). Note: track-level overrides are not part of the current v1 catalog; the Strand/Circle-scope surface is the only legitimate scope for a per-discussion override.

vectors.name: branch_overrides_loosen_rejected_when_not_allowed
vectors.comment: When the parent Realm declares scope_overrides_allowed=false, a Strand/Circle scope MUST NOT loosen the policy (Required→Optional, Private→Public, etc.). The sequenced-state transition rule rejects the loosening Move and keeps the parent value. Track-level override is not available (removed in v1) — the Strand/Circle-scope ak.realm.read_receipt_policy is the only surface.

vectors.name: prefs_resolution_strand_overrides_realm
vectors.comment: When policy is optional and the user has both parent-Realm-level and Strand/Circle-scope-level (Strand.scope_circle_id, AKP-0007) overrides, the Strand/Circle-scope override wins. Resolution order is strand → realm → default; track-level overrides are not in the current v1 catalog.

vectors.name: prefs_resolution_realm_overrides_default
vectors.comment: Without a Strand/Circle-scope-level override, the parent-Realm-level override wins over the default.
